description: ORVYX is a six-member team making space data accessible to everyone. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we're developing a web-based explorer for Planet X and SPHEREx. Users will search sky coordinates, compare infrared observations over time, and spot moving or changing celestial objects through interactive time-lapses. Our interests include astrophysics, software engineering, data analysis, AI, and visualization. We welcome builders and researchers who want to turn observations into discoveries.
summary:
ORVYX is an interactive time-domain and 102-band near-infrared discovery web application that transforms NASA’s SPHEREx archive into clear, evidence-linked astrophysical insights. Combining a 3D WebGL onboarding journey with a precision 2D Blink Observatory, ORVYX lets researchers, educators, and citizen scientists enter any sky coordinates (RA/Dec) or inspect the five mandatory NASA benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, R Draconis).

To address the challenge’s core physical hurdles—where fast-moving brown dwarfs like *WISE 0855* shift by only 0.65 pixels per six-month pass and Linear Variable Filters create wavelength gradients—our Python/FastAPI and Astropy pipeline performs automated WCS alignment, zodiacal background (`ZODI`) subtraction, bitmask flag filtering, subpixel centroid tracking, and on-the-fly 102-band spectral extraction. Synchronized Primary Blink and Paired Dipole Difference ($I_n - I_{\text{ref}}$) viewports cancel static stars to isolate moving and variable sources immediately.

ORVYX is vital because no human can manually inspect one billion objects across 102 infrared bands. By cross-matching NASA SPHEREx with ESA Gaia DR3 and CSA NEOSSat archives—paired with our citation-grounded AI **Cosmic Narrator**—ORVYX turns raw multi-agency telemetry into verifiable scientific discovery.
details:
ORVYX — SPHEREx Blink Observatory & Cosmic Narrator is an interactive time-domain and 102-band near-infrared discovery platform that turns NASA’s SPHEREx archive into evidence-linked astrophysical insights. Users enter sky coordinates (RA/Dec) via URL-queryable inputs or select one of the five mandatory NASA benchmark targets (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis).

Behind the scenes, ORVYX operates through a deterministic two-stage pipeline:

  • Astrophysical Processing & Alignment: The backend queries multi-epoch SPHEREx cutouts (QR3/QR2) via IRSA TAP/SIA protocols. Because spacecraft roll angles, zodiacal dust glow (ZODI), and Linear Variable Filter (LVF) wavelength gradients corrupt raw visual comparisons, our pipeline automatically reprojects images onto a unified World Coordinate System (WCS) grid, subtracts zodiacal background, masks cosmic-ray contamination via FLAGS bitmasks, and extracts source-specific wavelengths across the 102 channels (0.75–5.00 µm).
  • Subpixel Tracking, Dipole Subtraction & Multi-Agency Fusion: Using SEP (Source Extractor) ePSF centroiding, ORVYX tracks subpixel proper motion down to 0.65 pixels per six-month survey pass. The 2D workspace renders synchronized Primary Blink and Paired Dipole Difference ($I_n - I_{\text{ref}}$) viewports where stationary stars cancel out cleanly and moving objects appear as blue-to-amber dipoles. It simultaneously cross-matches sources against epoch-propagated ESA Gaia DR3 astrometry (flagging infrared-only optical dropouts) and CSA CADC NEOSSat near-Earth surveillance, while our Cosmic Narrator synthesizes measurements with SIMBAD and NASA ADS literature.

Benefits & Intended Impact SPHEREx images over one billion celestial objects every six months—a volume impossible to inspect manually for faint brown dwarfs, variable stars, or distant planetary candidates ("Planet X"). ORVYX bridges the gap between raw FITS archives and human discovery:

  • For Researchers: Provides instant WCS registration, WiseView-style Asinh radiometry stretching, on-the-fly 102-band spectral energy distribution (SED) plots, and shareable coordinate deep-links.
  • For Educators & Citizen Scientists: Replaces steep astronomical software barriers with an intuitive visual workflow that separates real physical motion or flux variability from instrumental noise.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

  • Backend & Science Pipeline: Python, FastAPI (Uvicorn ASGI), Astropy, Reproject, Astroquery, PyVO, SEP, NumPy, and SciPy (KDTree).
  • AI & Knowledge Layer: LangGraph, LangChain, and Pydantic structured outputs for our citation-grounded Agentic RAG pipeline, backed by PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Redis caching.
  • Frontend & Visual Engine: TypeScript, Node.js, React (Next.js/Vite), Tailwind CSS, HTML5 60fps Canvas, Three.js / @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, @react-three/postprocessing (ACES Filmic tone mapping, bloom, chromatic aberration, custom GLSL shaders), and GSAP.
  • Hardware: Developed and tested on a Windows 11 workstation equipped with an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 GPU for WebGL shader compilation and local pipeline execution.

How ORVYX Is Creative

  • 3D Narrative Onboarding to 2D Scientific Cockpit: Instead of dropping users directly into a complex FITS terminal, ORVYX opens with a scrollable 3D WebGL journey featuring sculptures of the SPHEREx spacecraft, infrared planetary atmospheres, and holographic observation plates before unmounting cleanly to launch a zero-latency 2D analysis observatory.
  • Strict Separation of Physics and AI: Rather than asking an LLM to guess whether a star moved, deterministic math computes the exact subpixel shift, SNR, and flux uncertainties first; the AI Cosmic Narrator then explains those verified numbers with clickable literature citations.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  1. The 0.65-Pixel Resolution Limit: At SPHEREx’s 6.2 arcsec/pixel scale, even WISE 0855 (moving at 8.14 arcsec/yr) shifts only ~0.65 pixels in six months—requiring subpixel zoom insets and dipole difference imaging rather than naive blinking.
  2. Wavelength-Matched Comparisons: Because SPHEREx uses Linear Variable Filters, we ensured brightness variability (RW Aurigae, R Draconis) is evaluated within matched spectral bands so spectral gradients are never mistaken for temporal variability.
  3. Epistemic Humility: Visual changes are treated as scientific leads rather than unverified discoveries, displaying contamination flags (contaminated=False), uncertainties, and candidate associations transparently.
